subject: maths
title: Adding and Subtracting Large Numbers
seo_title: Year 4 Adding and Subtracting Large Numbers Worksheets: Mental Strategies, Regrouping and Checking
standard_text: Develop efficient strategies and use appropriate digital tools for solving problems involving addition and subtraction, and multiplication and division where there is no remainder
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting 3-, 4- and 5-digit numbers, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N06): jump, split and compensate strategies, column addition and subtraction with regrouping, subtracting across zeros, checking with the inverse and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Choose a strategy: in your head if you can, in columns if you can’t.
key_sub: Mental strategies: jump, split or compensate (2999 is 3000 − 1). Columns: line up the ones, start on the right and regroup when you need to. Every 0 you regroup across becomes 9. Check with the inverse.
body_html:
The idea: use place value

Large numbers are made of ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Add or subtract the same places. When a place gets 10 or more, regroup: 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, and so on.

First ask: can I do this in my head? If not, use the column method.

Mental strategies

Jump: start at the first number and jump the thousands, then the hundreds, tens and ones.

Split: partition both numbers, add each place, then put the parts back together.

Compensate

What is 4625 + 2999?

2999 is 1 less than 3000. Add 3000: 4625 + 3000 = 7625. You added 1 too many, so take 1 away: 7624.

Answer: 7624

Column addition

Put ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on. Start on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

5-digit numbers

What is 36 478 + 25 865?

Ones: 8 + 5 = 13. Tens: 7 + 6 + 1 = 14. Hundreds: 4 + 8 + 1 = 13. Thousands: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12. Ten thousands: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

Answer: 62 343

Column subtraction, including across zeros

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column. If the next column is 0, go left to the first digit that is not 0. Every 0 you pass becomes 9.

Check with the inverse

Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check 5003 − 1478 = 3525, add: 3525 + 1478 = 5003. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not regrouping (4678 + 2856 = 6424)Write the regrouped 1 under the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (6152 − 2879 = 4727)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Not regrouping across zeros (5003 − 1478 = 3475)Go left to the first digit that is not 0. Each 0 you pass becomes 9
Lining up the numbers on the left (4567 + 382 = 8387)Line up the ones on the right: 4567 + 382 = 4949

faq.q: What does Year 4 learn about adding and subtracting in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Students choose efficient strategies to add and subtract larger numbers, such as jump, split and compensate in their heads, and the column method with regrouping. They also check answers with the inverse operation.
Round one number to a friendly number, work it out, then fix the difference. For 4625 + 2999, add 3000 to get 7625, then take away 1 to get 7624.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 5003 − 1478?
faq.a: Go left to the first digit that is not 0 and regroup from there; each 0 you pass becomes 9. 5003 becomes 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 13 ones, and the answer is 3525.

faq.q: How can my child check an addition or subtraction answer?
faq.a: Use the inverse: for 5003 − 1478 = 3525, check that 3525 + 1478 = 5003. If you get back to the starting number, the answer is right.

items.q: A stadium has 50 000 seats. 37 468 people come to a rugby league match. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 50 000 − 37 468 = 12 532. Check: 12 532 + 37 468 = 50 000.

items.q: The crowd at a footy final was 91 526. The crowd at the first match of the season was 47 835. How many more people were at the final?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 91 526 − 47 835 = 43 691. Check: 43 691 + 47 835 = 91 526.

items.q: On a road trip, a family drove 1286 km in the first week and 1947 km in the second week. How far did they drive altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 1286 + 1947 = 3233. Check: 3233 − 1947 = 1286.

items.q: Mia’s family is driving 14 500 km around Australia. They have driven 8763 km. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Find the distance left, so subtract. 14 500 − 8763 = 5737. Check: 5737 + 8763 = 14 500.

items.q: At the start of a road trip, the car’s odometer showed 45 208 km. At the end it showed 47 135 km. How far did the car travel?
items.e: Find the difference between the two readings, so subtract. 47 135 − 45 208 = 1927. Check: 1927 + 45 208 = 47 135.

items.q: The school fete raised $4385 and the walkathon raised $2768. How much money was raised altogether?
The P&C wants to raise $10 000 for a new shade sail. It has raised $6475. How much more does it need?
items.e: Find the difference, so subtract. $10 000 − $6475 = $3525. Check: $3525 + $6475 = $10 000.

items.q: A swimming club raised $12 475 last year. This year it raised $9638. How much did it raise in the two years?
items.e: Put the two years together, so add. $12 475 + $9638 = $22 113. Check: $22 113 − $9638 = $12 475.

items.q: A charity fun run had 23 150 runners. 18 674 of them finished in under an hour. How many runners took an hour or more?
items.e: Take away the runners who finished in under an hour. 23 150 − 18 674 = 4476. Check: 4476 + 18 674 = 23 150.

items.q: A stadium has 60 000 seats. 28 375 tickets were sold online and 14 690 were sold at the gate. How many seats are still empty?
The crowd at a netball grand final was 16 245. The crowd at a footy match was 8538 more than that. How many people went to the two matches altogether?
items.e: Step 1, the footy crowd: 16 245 + 8538 = 24 783. Step 2, both together: 16 245 + 24 783 = 41 028.

items.q: A cricket match had a crowd of 42 718 on day 1. On day 2, the crowd was 9465 smaller. How many people came on the two days?
A family is driving 4000 km from Perth to Sydney. They drove 1348 km on the first two days and 1275 km on the next two days. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Step 1, kilometres driven: 1348 + 1275 = 2623. Step 2, kilometres left: 4000 − 2623 = 1377.

items.q: Oliver’s family drove 2386 km to Darwin and 1958 km on day trips. Ava’s family drove 5000 km on their holiday. How many more kilometres did Ava’s family drive?
items.e: Step 1, Oliver’s family: 2386 + 1958 = 4344. Step 2, find the difference: 5000 − 4344 = 656.

items.q: A school had $8326 in its sport fund. It spent $3458 on new netballs and footballs. Then a sausage sizzle raised $1275. How much money is in the fund now?
items.e: Step 1, after spending: $8326 − $3458 = $4868. Step 2, after the sausage sizzle: $4868 + $1275 = $6143.

items.q: A school wants to raise $15 000 for new library books. The fete raised $6247 and a trivia night raised $3865. How much more does the school need?
items.e: Step 1, money raised: $6247 + $3865 = $10 112. Step 2, money still needed: $15 000 − $10 112 = $4888.

items.q: Cooper’s class raised $1450 in a readathon. Mia’s class raised $375 less. How much did the two classes raise altogether?
A footy club sold 12 486 tickets to members and 9725 tickets to the public. The ground holds 25 000 people. How many more tickets can be sold?
items.e: Step 1, tickets sold: 12 486 + 9725 = 22 211. Step 2, find the difference: 25 000 − 22 211 = 2789.

items.q: A charity had 4062 tins of food. It gave out 2785 tins. Then a school food drive brought in 1938 tins. How many tins does the charity have now?
items.e: Step 1, after giving out: 4062 − 2785 = 1277. Step 2, after the food drive: 1277 + 1938 = 3215.
